claims.text: The initial material is a fine-grained FeNiCrCoCu thin-film protective coating on a conventional metal substrate.
A controlled pre-oxidation treatment below 500°C will promote early formation of a coherent oxide scale on FeNiCrCoCu.
Pre-oxidation will produce a continuous, stable oxide layer along the coating surface and grain boundaries.
The resulting oxide layer will adhere strongly to the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The oxide layer will shift high-temperature wear from direct metallic adhesive and abrasive wear to behavior governed by a protective oxide scale.
The oxide layer protects against direct metal-to-metal contact.
The oxide layer acts as a sacrificial barrier during sliding contact.
The oxide barrier reduces local friction as temperature increases.
The oxide barrier reduces adhesive wear.
The oxide barrier reduces abrasive wear.
Pre-oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coatings will have a significantly lower wear rate than untreated coatings at elevated temperature.
Pre-oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coatings will have a lower coefficient of friction than untreated coatings at elevated temperature.
Worn pre-oxidized surfaces will retain a coherent, finely dispersed oxide scale.
The proposed mechanism applies to thin FeNiCrCoCu coatings at temperatures up to approximately 500°C under service-like wear loads.
The relevant oxide composition, thickness, adhesion strength, and interaction with grain boundaries have not yet been fully characterized under the proposed conditions.
Failure to obtain statistically significant reductions in both wear rate and coefficient of friction, or oxide spallation that increases wear, would falsify the hypothesis.
